Subject: Model fit & prompt collection: next steps and prompt set request

Hi Sofia / Diego —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side: 

1) Recap from discovery:
- Primary product: ACME Assist chat + automated response generation for support tickets (English, en-US)
- Target latency: sub-700ms p95 for short replies (<= 150 tokens)
- Primary concern: hallucination on policy/procurement content and PII handling for refund/financial inquiries
- Expected volume: ~1.2M tokens/month initially; peak 3x during promotions

2) Redwood recommendations (high-level):
- Models to evaluate first: Llama 3 32B quantized int8 (for higher-context accuracy) and Mistral 7B-v2 finetuned on instruction-following (cost-optimized)
- Initial evals: run the provided prompt set against both models + our safety reranker; collect precision/recall on factual answers and hallucination rate on a 200-case benchmark

3) Immediate ask from ACME: prompt set collection + edge cases
- Please send: a representative sample (50–150 prompts) across ticket types (billing, technical, account changes), including the edge cases you care about (redactions, ambiguous references, multi-turn clarifications).
- Sensitive data guidance: redact direct identifiers (SSNs, full credit card numbers). You can use placeholders like [REDACTED_CUST_ID] or <CC_LAST4=1234>. If you need, we can provide a small redaction script.

I attached a prompt collection template (acme_prompt_collection_template.csv) and an example edge-case file to make this easy. 

Next steps / timeline:
- Sofia shares prompt set by EOD Fri 7/10 (would be ideal)
- We run an initial model-fit eval and share benchmark links + recommended config by Tue 7/14
- Schedule a follow-up demo of the best-fit model and latency testing — Vivek and Rishi will join for the deep-dive.

If the timeline is tight, even 30 representative prompts will let us produce a quick model-fit signal.

Thanks — looking forward.

—
Marissa Cole

Thanks Marissa — great recap and really helpful template. A couple quick clarifications before we pull the set: 

1) Format: we can export CSV from Zendesk, but do you prefer free-text examples (one prompt per line) or the table with metadata (ticket type, priority, redact flag)?
2) Redaction: we can replace emails and CC numbers with placeholders. For account numbers we have both full and masked values — should we keep masked (XXX-1234) or replace entirely?
3) Edge cases: we have about 20 known problem tickets where the model historically hallucinated product availability or mixed up SLA terms. We'll include those.

We'll try to get 100 examples by Friday. For the immediate eval, is it okay if some prompts are anonymized (removed customer identifiers) but still include the ticket context?

On the model side: can you share the benchmark doc you mentioned so Diego and our ML lead can review before Tuesday?

Thanks — Sofia

Hi Sofia — great questions. Quick answers inline and added a few practical tips below.

1) Format: the template CSV with columns (prompt_text, ticket_type, priority, redact_flag, notes) is ideal because it helps us automatically slice and analyze. Free-text is fine for quick starts but will take extra manual tagging.

2) Redaction: keep masked values where possible (e.g., XXXX-1234) — that preserves the token shapes and is helpful for model evaluation. For anything regulated (full CC, SSN), fully redact and use placeholders like <REDACTED_SSN>. Mark redact_flag=TRUE in the CSV.

3) Anonymization: fully acceptable. Preserve context (ticket thread excerpt) but strip PII. If you're worried about losing semantics, include a short "context_notes" column describing the omitted values (e.g., customer asked about invoice showing charge for MONTHLY_PLUS plan).

Benchmarks: attaching the Redwood model comparison PDF (redwood_model_benchmarks_q2_2026.pdf) — contains baseline latency/cost/quality for the models we recommended (Llama 3 32B int8, Mistral 7B-v2, and a tuned 13B variant). Key pages: pages 6–9 show hallucination rates on our public support-ticket benchmark.

Edge-case guidance: include the examples where you saw hallucinations and mark them as "edgecase" in the ticket_type column. For hallucination assessment we'll run an automated checklist then a small manual review (10% sample) to calculate false-positive factual answers.

Attachments: acme_prompt_collection_template.csv (template), example_edgecase_prompts.txt (sample).

Proposed next steps: 
- Sofia to share CSV by EOD Fri 7/10 (even anonymized)
- We ingest and run model-fit eval across 3 model candidates by Tue 7/14 and share an evaluation dashboard link + recommended config
- Schedule a 45-min follow-up on Wed 7/15 for a demo with latency tests (Vivek + Rishi)

If helpful, Rishi can put together a short checklist for redaction automation and runbook for on-prem/private data handling. Chloe will also loop in the Solutions team for SSO/KMS questions if this moves forward.

Best,
Marissa

Attachments: redwood_model_benchmarks_q2_2026.pdf, acme_prompt_collection_template.csv
